title: Decimal Point
statement:
You are given a positive integer S. Consider its decimal representation as a string of digits.

Your task is to generate all possible valid decimal representations by inserting exactly one decimal point (.) at every possible position.

The decimal point can be placed:

1. Before the first digit, in which case prefix the number with 0.
   - Example: 123 -> 0.123

2. Between any two consecutive digits.
   - Example: 123 -> 1.23, 12.3

3. After the last digit, in which case append .0.
   - Example: 123 -> 123.0

Return all generated decimal representations as a single space-separated string, in the above order.

Input Format:
- input1: A positive integer S.

Output Format:
- Print a single string containing all possible decimal representations separated by a single space.

examples.explanation:
Possible positions of decimal point:
- Before first digit -> 0.123
- Between 1 and 2 -> 1.23
- Between 2 and 3 -> 12.3
- After last digit -> 123.0

Since there is only one digit, there is no position between digits.
Possible representations are:
- Before the digit -> 0.5
- After the digit -> 5.0

hints: Convert integer S to its string representation str.
Then loop i from 1 to str.length() - 1, slicing substring(0, i) + '.' + substring(i).
discussion: Simple string manipulation problem generating all 1-point insertions in O(|S|) time.
